title: How to Interview Fractional Recruiters (November 2026)
summary: Interview fractional recruiters in three simple steps: get ready, cover the right topics on a free call, and pick the best fit. Updated November 2026.
body_markdown:
Most founders get one or two short calls to decide who will own a search. The good news: you don’t need a long list of questions. Get your search ready, cover a handful of topics on each call, and pick the recruiter you trust. This guide covers[how to interview fractional recruiters](https://www.dover.com/) in three steps.


**TLDR:**


- Treat every intro call as a real interview, and keep it simple: prep, five topics, a decision.
- Know your role, timeline, budget and where your search stands before the first call.
- Many searches fail at closing, not sourcing, so ask how a recruiter plans the offer stage.
- Most companies talk to about four recruiters before choosing one. Trial more than one and keep the best fit.


## Interviewing a Fractional Recruiter in Three Steps


### 1. Get your search ready


Spend 15 minutes writing down the basics. The more clearly you can describe the search, the more accurately a recruiter can tell you what is realistic.


- The role: must-have skills, nice-to-haves and deal-breakers
- Timeline: target start date, shortlist deadline and who makes the decision
- Budget: what you plan to spend and where you want the most help
- Where you are today: your job description, channels you’ve tried and any candidates in process


Don’t worry if some of it is still fuzzy. Just say so. A good recruiter will help you sharpen it.


### 2. Talk to a few recruiters


Intro calls are free, so talk to a few. Be candid, because recruiters on Dover only take on searches they believe can succeed. You don’t need a script. Cover these five topics:


- **Availability:** how many hours they have for your roles and how often they’ll update you
- **Relevant experience:** similar roles at a similar company stage, with specific examples
- **Plan:** what they’d do in the first week, where they’ll source and a realistic timeline for making the hire based on the current hiring market
- **Process:** how they’ll work with you, and which parts of the hiring process they’ll handle versus your team
- **Closing:** how they handle competing offers and late-stage objections


### 3. Pick recruiters and get started


After a call, you should be able to say yes to most of these:


- They can restate your role and constraints clearly
- Their plan and timeline sound realistic
- They have the hours and relevant experience you need
- They’re easy to talk to and willing to push back
- You’d enjoy working with them


If several recruiters look strong, work with a couple. You can switch recruiters any time, and you can set a weekly or monthly budget so you stay in control of your costs.

## FAQs


### Should you ask a fractional recruiter for references?


Yes. References are most useful when they come from hiring managers or founders at a similar company stage, since they can speak to how the recruiter handled speed, feedback loops and closing. On Dover, verified founder reviews on each recruiter’s profile give you a head start.


### How is fractional recruiting different from agency recruiting?


Agency recruiters usually work on contingency and charge a percentage of first-year salary per placement. Fractional recruiters are typically billed hourly or per hire and work inside your process, often owning sourcing, interview coordination and closing alongside your team.


### Do you need an ATS before bringing in a fractional recruiter?


Not strictly, but a shared ATS makes the engagement easier. The recruiter and your team see the same pipeline, notes and feedback in real time, and the candidate history stays with your company if the engagement ends. Dover pairs a free ATS with on-demand fractional recruiters, and many recruiters can also work inside tools a team already uses.


## Final Thoughts on Interviewing Fractional Recruiters


Knowing[how to interview fractional recruiters](https://www.dover.com/) comes down to prepping the basics, covering a few topics, and choosing the person you trust to run your search. Dover is one place to start: a free ATS, free intro calls with fractional recruiters, and no long-term contract.
